Tabil — The Tunisian Spice of the Coriander Seed

Tunisian · Easy · Makes about 50 g (about ⅓ cup and a spoon)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The tabil is Tunisian cooking's own fingerprint — the coriander-and-caraway-garlic blend ("tabil" is the Tunisian Arabic's own word for coriander itself) that runs the loubia pots, the kefta's spice, the octopus's braises, and the #43 and #88's bean doctrine. Where the Moroccan pot runs the ras el hanout's council (#94), the Tunisian pot runs this single decisive trio.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • the coastal school's warmth
- **The tabil's law: the coriander runs the blend's majority, and the garlic runs dry.** The blend's name is the coriander's own — the seed's citrus-earth runs two-thirds of the jar's weight — and the garlic, in the truest register, runs the dried clove's concentration (the fresh-run version runs the paste's moisture and the jar's shorter life, honestly labeled the modern mercy). - **The bridge:** the #94's council-of-fifteen and this trio run the two kitchens' own philosophies at the same cupboard — the Moroccan blend's perfume democracy and the Tunisian blend's decisive hierarchy — and the corpus's bean-and-sausage seats (#43, #88, the kefta's #33) carry this jar's every citation.

Tabil — The Tunisian Spice of the Coriander Seed

Prep: 10 min · Cook: 8 min · Total: 18 min · Makes about 50 g (about ⅓ cup and a spoon)

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 3 tbsp coriander seeds (about 18 g)
  • 1 tbsp caraway seeds (about 7 g)
  • 6 garlic cloves (about 24 g), the dried-day's honesty or the fresh's mercy
  • 1 tsp cayenne or 1 tsp harissa's dried-register (about 3 g), the heat's own dial
  • ½ tsp ground cinnamon (about 1.5 g), optional — the coastal school's warmth

Instructions

  1. **The toast (5–6 minutes).** The coriander and caraway toasted dry in the heavy pan over the medium-low — the pan's steady swirl — to the coriander's fragrance's first full bloom and the seeds' faint gold: the citrus-earth's perfume rising warm, the caraway's anise-sharp edge softening behind. Checkpoint — the toast's edge, the #94's own law carried: the nose's first peak is the pan's off-moment — the coriander's scorch runs the blend's whole bitterness, and the pepper's sneeze provocation at the pan's face is the toast's own honest clock.
  2. **The garlic's dry-run (optional, the traditional register).** The garlic cloves, peeled and sliced, dried a day at the counter's air (or the oven's lowest's 20 minutes at 90 °C's mercy) to the leathery concentration — or run the fresh's shortcut honestly, the blend's processor route. Checkpoint — the dried clove's law: the slice's bend without the snap — the leathery stage between the fresh's moisture and the crisp's bone; the dried garlic's concentration runs the blend's shelf-honesty, and the fresh's blend runs the week's own jar.
  3. **The grind.** The toasted seeds cooled 5 minutes and ground with the garlic and the cayenne (the cinnamon's option following) to the fine, even powder — the mortar's ten minutes' tradition or the spice mill's three short bursts. Checkpoint — eating test (the oil's bloom, the blend's own workshop): a pinch of the tabil dropped into the warm oil's shimmer — the bloom's perfume rising (the coriander's citrus-earth forward, the caraway's signature at the lift, the garlic's warmth rounding) — and the fingertip's taste: the heat present, the coriander's majority honest, the blend's whole running decisive rather than the council's democratic murmur. It should taste like the Tunisian pot's own opening chord — the same three notes the #43 and the #88 run, stated once at the jar's law.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Blend bitterThe coriander's scorchThe nose's first-peak law
Blend's perfume flatThe pre-ground corianderThe whole seed's toast-and-grind — the blend's whole point
Jar's clumping, short lifeThe fresh garlic's moistureThe dried register — or the week's own honest use

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The dried-garlic jar keeps 2 months at the sealed dark's cool; the fresh-garlic jar runs the week's honest register, the refrigerator's mercy. The variations: the Sfax school's hotter hand (the cayenne's doubling), the cinnamon's coastal warmth, the mint's dried whisper of the summer blend.
